reasons: The proposed hot food takeaway would be located in Hexthorpe and Balby North Ward, which has 23 hot food takeaways, equal to about 1.89 per 1,000 population against a national average of 0.96. The ward is therefore well above the national average. It also has high levels of child obesity (33.6% of Year 6 children obese) and high deprivation. Further hot food provision would harm efforts to promote healthier communities and would add to an existing over-concentration of takeaways. This is a locational test that conditions or changes to the layout cannot overcome. The proposal is contrary to Doncaster Local Plan Policies 24 and 50 and NPPF paragraphs 96 and 97.

The principle of reusing a vacant 24 m² commercial unit within the Doncaster Main Urban Area is considered acceptable in itself. No extension or new access is proposed, and the scale is well below the NPPF impact-assessment threshold. This is in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 1 and NPPF paragraphs 91 and 94. It does not outweigh the harm identified in relation to public health and the concentration of hot food takeaways.

The proposal is considered acceptable in highways and parking terms. There would be no new or altered access and no change to the existing parking area. Highways advise that the takeaway would generate a similar level of use to the taxi office. There would be no unacceptable highway safety impact or severe cumulative impact, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 13 and NPPF paragraphs 115 and 116.

Land contamination is not considered to be a constraint. The application states that there is no known or suspected contamination, the unit is existing and no groundworks are proposed. This is in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 54 and NPPF paragraph 187. Because the application is refused on public health grounds, the submitted information on noise and odour from the extraction system has not been taken further.
